title: Positive monoid finiteness and the mixed ideal filtration
statement:
Let $P\subseteq G$ be a finitely generated additive submonoid of an abelian group, and let $w:G	o\mathbf Z$ be a homomorphism with $w(p)>0$ for $p\in P\setminus\{0\}$. For $p\in P$, let $L(p)$ be the set of integers $q\ge0$ for which $p$ is a sum of $q$ nonzero elements of $P$, with the empty sum equal to $0$. Then $L(p)$ has a largest element $
u(p)$, $
u(0)=0$, $
u(p)\le w(p)$, and $
u(u)+
u(v)\le
u(u+v)$. For every integer $M\ge0$ the set $\{p\in P:w(p)\le M\}$ is finite. For every $p\in P$ and integer $k\ge1$, the set of tuples $(p_1,\ldots,p_k)\in P^k$ with $\sum_i p_i=p$ is finite. For every integer $n\ge1$, the set $S_n=\{p\in P:
u(p)<n\}$ is finite. Let $A$ be any commutative ring and $I\subseteq A$ any ideal. Write $A[P]$ for the monoid algebra of [def-trf-complete-toric-model] (zero polynomial variables), namely the finite sums $\sum_p c_pz^p$ with multiplication $z^uz^v=z^{u+v}$, and let $J=(I z^0,z^p:p
e0)$ be the generated ideal. For each $n\ge1$ and each $F=\sum_p c_pz^p\in A[P]$, one has
$$F\in J^n\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad c_p\in I^{\max(n-
u(p),0)}	ext{ for every }p\in P.$$
Here $I^j$ is the ideal of finite sums of products of $j$ elements of $I$, and $I^0=A$.

source.place: Exposé VI §1.6(i)--(ii), printed p. 70: agent-supplied coefficient refinement of the formal monoid models; not a verbatim theorem of ILO.

proof.text: Each nonzero element has integral weight at least one. Applying the weight homomorphism to a Fin q decomposition bounds q by w(p), hence by w(p).toNat. The set of lengths is nonempty (empty at zero and singleton away from zero), so Mathlib's BddAbove.exists_isGreatest_of_nonempty supplies an attained maximum ν(p). Choose these maxima; their weight bound implies ν(0)=0. Concatenate attaining tuples with Fin.append and Fin.sum_univ_add to prove ν(a)+ν(b)≤ν(a+b).

source.place: Exposé VI §1.6(i)--(ii), printed p. 70: agent-supplied coefficient refinement of the formal monoid models; not a verbatim theorem of ILO.

proof.text: Transfer finite generation to the monoid P itself and choose a finite generating set. Erase zero without changing its additive closure. Closure induction expresses every element as the sum of a finite list with entries in this finite set S. Each list yields an attained nonzero-summand decomposition of its sum. If w(p)≤M, its length is ≤w(p)≤M, so p lies in the image under summation of the finite set of S-lists of length ≤M.toNat. If ν(p)<n, the same list has length ≤ν(p)<n, so the finite set of S-lists of length <n surjects onto the length sublevel set. These arguments include S empty.

source.place: Exposé VI §1.6(i)--(ii), printed p. 70: agent-supplied coefficient refinement of the formal monoid models; not a verbatim theorem of ILO.

proof.text: For a tuple of sum p, each entry has weight at most w(p), since all the other weights are nonnegative. Thus such tuples form a subset of a finite Cartesian power of the weight sublevel set. This proves the tuple finiteness clause (even in length zero).

source.place: Exposé VI §1.6(i)--(ii), printed p. 70: agent-supplied coefficient refinement of the formal monoid models; not a verbatim theorem of ILO.

proof.text: For any commutative additive monoid equipped with the attained maximum length ν, zero length at zero, and superadditivity, define K_n to consist of finite coefficient families F with F.coeff(p)∈I^(n-ν(p)). This is an ideal: addition is coefficientwise; for multiplication by an arbitrary polynomial use the finite convolution formula, ν(b)≤ν(a+b), and antitonicity of ideal powers. Likewise K_m K_n⊆K_(m+n): for each convolution term use (m+n)-ν(a+b)≤(m-ν(a))+(n-ν(b)), multiplication of coefficient ideal powers, and closure under finite sums. This is a genuine ideal construction, with all closure properties proved.

source.place: Exposé VI §1.6(i)--(ii), printed p. 70: agent-supplied coefficient refinement of the formal monoid models; not a verbatim theorem of ILO.

proof.text: The mixed ideal J is contained in K_1. A coefficient generator single(0,a) has coefficient a∈I at zero and zero elsewhere, using ν(0)=0. For a nonzero monomial generator single(p,1), a singleton decomposition gives ν(p)≥1, so its only nonzero coefficient is unrestricted in I^0. Induction on n, using J^(n+1)=J^n J and K_n K_1⊆K_(n+1), proves J^n⊆K_n, including n=0.

source.place: Exposé VI §1.6(i)--(ii), printed p. 70: agent-supplied coefficient refinement of the formal monoid models; not a verbatim theorem of ILO.

proof.text: For the reverse inclusion, the constant ring homomorphism C:a↦single(0,a) maps I into J; Ideal.map_pow and monotonicity of ideal powers give C(I^k)⊆J^k. A decomposition attaining r=ν(p) gives single(p,1)∈J^r by multiplying its r nonzero monomials; the empty product covers r=0. Thus c∈I^(n-r) implies single(p,c)=C(c) single(p,1)∈J^((n-r)+r)⊆J^n, since n≤(n-r)+r. This uniformly treats r<n and r≥n without splitting or grouping tuples into blocks. Finally sum these monomials over the finite support of F. Combine the algebraic equivalence with the three finiteness clauses and the maximal-length properties, preserving the theorem's statement exactly.

source.place: Exposé VI §1.6(i)--(ii), printed p. 70: agent-supplied coefficient refinement of the formal monoid models; not a verbatim theorem of ILO.
